newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt share prices continue to score record gains.
newsitem.headline: Egypt share prices continue to score record gains.

text.p: Egyptian share prices continued to score record gains on Thursday in trade dominated by milling and cement sectors.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index rose 3.3 points to 272.27 on Thursday, up from 268.97 on Wednesday. The index has been climbing since Sunday when it first broke the previous record of 255.05 set in October 1994.
Brokers were upbeat after the record week.
"The market is great regardless of what is said - that it might correct itself. It's killing any doubt this market might go down in the short term," said broker Elwy Taymour at EFG Hermes.
Cement and milling firms took their usual places at the top of the list in terms of highest turnover and share price rises.
Taymour attributed the strong mills performances in general to the fact that mills have moved into producing profitable 72 extraction flour.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills led turnover with 3.66 million pounds changing hands. The share's price rose 5.90 pounds to close at 87.00.

General Silos and Storage was next with 3.53 million pounds turnover, ending up 0.65 at 50.75 pounds. Upper Egypt Flour Mills followed with 3.43 million pounds in turnover and a closing price of 74.20, a 0.20 pound rise.
Mohammad Hamed of Okaz Stockbrokers and Investment Consultants said: "Milling shares are making good profits. Also, Suez Cement is up because of the information about the GDR."

Suez Cement gained 0.05 pounds to 56.50 in trade of 1.65 million pounds. Trade has been spurred by Tuesday's transfer of 7.75 million shares worth 387.5 million pounds into a global depository receipt offering (GDR).
An 8.24 percent jump in the National Cement share price made it the day's biggest gainer. The share price closed at 22.80 pounds.
Of a total 75 stocks traded, 26 rose, 17 fell and the rest closed unchanged.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 419.9 points from 409.15 on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 188.67 points from 187.91 points.
